text:
kevin_support: Hey team — customer on Private deployment reporting streaming websocket sessions randomly stop sending tokens after ~70-120s. Client still shows socket open but no data for ~90s, then reconnect. Happens only from their VPC egress subnet, not public tests. Repro steps below.

kevin_support: Repro steps: 1) Start hosted stream via our API from a VM in their VPC (curl + websocat). 2) Send a prompt that streams ~10s of tokens. 3) After ~1-2 minutes stream stalls (no chunks) even though server thinks it is still generating. We only see final reconnect from the client.

kevin_support: Quick log snippet from their proxy: `2026-01-12T14:22:08 proxy[pid]: conn 10.x.x.x:443 -> buffer_coalesce: 2048 bytes; idle 85s; state=established`

jonah_escalations: Thanks Kevin — can you confirm whether they're terminating TLS in a corporate middlebox (TLS inspection) or if we see passthrough? Also which egress appliance (F5, Palo Alto, BlueCoat, cloud NAT) is in front?

kevin_support: They are using an on-prem security appliance that does TLS rewrap (company policy). They said it's a Palo Alto cluster with traffic steering. Egress IPs are in their allowlist.

maria_neteng: This reads like middlebox-induced buffering / TCP coalescing + an idle timeout. Middleboxes that do TLS interception often buffer small outbound frames then flush based on either timer or when they see enough bytes. That causes long gaps from client POV even though server pushes tokens.

maria_neteng: Two quick checks: 1) Can you get a tcpdump from VM to appliance and from appliance to our endpoint to see whether packets leave the appliance in a steady stream or in bursts? 2) Can we confirm if the appliance rewrites TLS records (TLS length changes) or performs any HTTP/2/ALPN translation?

kevin_support: I asked customer for tcpdumps on both sides — they sent the one between VM -> appliance: it shows small TLS records from client frequently, then nothing while server-side logs show continuous generation. They didn't provide appliance -> internet capture yet.

jonah_escalations: In the interim, try this mitigation: enable WS-level pings from the client (send a 1-byte application frame or WebSocket Ping every 30s). That forces the middlebox to flush and resets timers. Also try disabling Nagle on the client side (TCP_NODELAY) and set TLS record size to avoid coalescing.

kevin_support: Noted. Customer asked for a change that doesn't require app dev work — any infra workaround?

maria_neteng: If they control the appliance, ask them to whitelist our destination and enable passthrough for that IP range or reduce the TLS buffering threshold. On many Palo Alto boxes there is an "SSL forward proxy" buffer timeout you can tune. If it's a managed FW (ISP) they may need to disable deep-packet inspection for the API host.

jonah_escalations: Also check keepalive at TCP level — linux `sysctl` tcp_keepalive_time/interval probes can help but are much coarser. WebSocket ping is simplest and effective.

kevin_support: Customer is testing a WebSocket ping patch now. They asked whether Redwood can change server behavior (e.g., emit extra padding frames or periodic noop tokens) while we wait for their fix.

jonah_escalations: We can experiment with emitting a 1-byte padding token every 25s for Private customers behind known middleboxes, but that's a product change. For now I recommended they enable pings. I'll escalate to product to discuss an opt-in server-side keepalive toggle for Private deployments.

maria_neteng: One more diagnostic: if their appliance is doing TLS rewrap, have them capture the TLS version/cipher on both sides — sometimes rewrap causes record-aggregation bugs. If you get the appliance->internet tcpdump and it still shows bursts, then it's definitely the middlebox.

kevin_support: Got it. Customer confirmed pings reduced incidents in a 24h smoke test (no stalls so far). They will keep appliance config change queued. I'll log follow-up with product for server-side toggle. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
